claims.sentence: On 17 September 2026 the WHO described the safety themes of its forthcoming asthma guidelines, which have not yet been published.
claims.evidence: Page URL dated 17-09-2026, title "Patient safety at the heart of forthcoming WHO asthma guidelines"; retrieved text describes the guidance as not yet published.

claims.sentence: The WHO published the article on 17 September 2026, linked to World Patient Safety Day.
claims.evidence: Date 17 September 2026 confirmed by URL. The World Patient Safety Day link came only from a blended search summary that also drew on the separate WPSD 2026 calls-to-action page; I cannot tell the news item itself says it.
claims.newSentence: The WHO published the article on 17 September 2026.

claims.sentence: The WHO estimates that asthma affected about 363 million people in 2023 and caused 442,000 deaths.
claims.evidence: Retrieved text: "Asthma affected an estimated 363 million people in 2023 and caused 442 000 deaths", attributed to the 17 Sept 2026 news item.

claims.sentence: The WHO links overuse of reliever inhalers with more asthma attacks and deaths.
claims.evidence: "Reliever inhaler overuse has been associated with increased rates of asthma attacks and mortality" (WHO news item). "Links" is slightly stronger than "associated"; acceptable.

claims.sentence: The forthcoming guidance stresses shared decision-making, correct use of inhalers and devices, continuity of care and follow-up after severe attacks.
claims.evidence: The wording on shared decision-making, correct use of medicines/devices, continuity of care and follow-up after severe attacks came from a summary that cited the WPSD 2026 calls-to-action page; could not confirm the news item itself states it.

claims.sentence: On 17 September 2026 the World Health Organization (WHO) published an article on patient safety in its forthcoming asthma guidelines. The guidelines themselves have not yet been published.
claims.evidence: News item dated 17 Sept 2026 about forthcoming guidelines; guidelines described as not yet published.

claims.sentence: The WHO estimates that asthma affected about 363 million people in 2023 and caused 442,000 deaths.
claims.evidence: Same figures quoted from the news item: 363 million in 2023, 442 000 deaths.

claims.sentence: It says overusing reliever inhalers is linked to more asthma attacks and deaths.
claims.evidence: Overuse "associated with increased rates of asthma attacks and mortality" attributed to WHO item.

claims.sentence: It also cites a Global Asthma Network survey in which 45% to 60% of people with severe symptoms were not taking inhaled corticosteroids, with larger gaps in lower-income settings.
claims.evidence: Summary of the item: Global Asthma Network survey, 45% to 60% of people with severe symptoms not taking inhaled corticosteroids depending on age group, larger gaps in lower-income settings (quote from Prof Refiloe Masekela). Reported as WHO relaying the survey, matching the sentence.

claims.sentence: The WHO says the forthcoming guidance aims to strengthen evidence-based care and reduce avoidable harm.
claims.evidence: "WHO's forthcoming asthma guidance aims to strengthen evidence-based care and reduce avoidable harm" appears as the page wording.

claims.sentence: It stresses shared decision-making, correct use of inhalers and devices, continuity of care, and follow-up after severe attacks.
claims.evidence: Same issue as key point 4: themes retrieved from the WPSD 2026 calls-to-action text, not clearly from the news item. Note one summary says guidance is due early 2027 (not in the brief).
